description: Question bank on Natural Disasters and Disaster Management (Unit 3.11) prepared from the Comprehensive Question-Answer Study Material. Verify and expand before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: A disaster is best defined as:

options.A: Any natural event that occurs on Earth
options.B: A serious disruption of a community's functioning causing losses that exceed its own coping capacity
options.C: Any rainfall above the normal average
options.D: A hazard that occurs in a populated area

questions.explanation: A disaster is a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or society causing widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses that exceed the affected community's ability to cope using its own resources.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a hazard?

options.A: A disaster that has already occurred
options.B: A potentially damaging event or process
options.C: The inability of a community to cope
options.D: The measure of losses from an event

questions.explanation: A hazard is a potentially damaging event or process. It becomes a disaster only when it seriously disrupts a community and exceeds its coping capacity.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines exposure in disaster risk analysis?

options.A: The physical, social and economic conditions that increase susceptibility to harm
options.B: The people, assets and ecosystems located in harm's way
options.C: The strengths and resources available to cope and recover
options.D: The potential for loss arising from a hazard

questions.explanation: Exposure refers to people, assets and ecosystems located in harm's way. Vulnerability is the set of conditions that increase susceptibility to harm.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Vulnerability in disaster management refers to:

options.A: The location of people and assets in harm's way
options.B: The physical, social, economic and environmental conditions that increase susceptibility to harm
options.C: The resources available to anticipate and recover
options.D: The magnitude of the triggering hazard

questions.explanation: Vulnerability is the set of physical, social, economic and environmental conditions that increase susceptibility to harm.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Capacity in disaster risk analysis refers to:

options.A: The strength of a hazard
options.B: The strengths and resources available to anticipate, cope and recover
options.C: The number of people exposed to a hazard
options.D: The total economic loss from a disaster

questions.explanation: Capacity is the strengths and resources available to anticipate, cope and recover from a hazard event.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Disaster risk is the potential for loss arising from the interaction of:

options.A: Hazard and magnitude only
options.B: Hazard, exposure, vulnerability and capacity
options.C: Exposure and population density only

questions.explanation: Disaster risk depends on hazard, exposure, vulnerability and capacity. Not every hazard becomes a disaster.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement about hazards and disasters?

options.A: Every hazard automatically becomes a disaster
options.B: A hazard becomes a disaster only when it seriously disrupts a community and exceeds its coping capacity
options.C: A disaster is always caused only by natural processes
options.D: Hazards and disasters are identical terms

questions.explanation: A hazard is a potentially damaging event; a disaster occurs when the event seriously disrupts a community and exceeds its capacity to cope using its own resources. Not every hazard becomes a disaster.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: By origin, disasters are classified as:

options.A: Sudden and slow-onset
options.B: Natural and human-induced
options.C: Geological and biological

questions.explanation: Disasters may be classified by origin (natural or human-induced), process, speed of onset, duration, scale and affected sector.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which classification of disasters is based on the nature of the process?

options.A: Sudden-onset and slow-onset
options.B: Geological, hydrological, meteorological, climatological and biological
options.C: Local, regional and national

questions.explanation: Disasters may be classified by process as geological, hydrological, meteorological, climatological or biological.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides and tsunamis are examples of which type of hazard?

options.A: Hydrological
options.B: Meteorological
options.C: Geological

questions.explanation: Geological hazards include earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides, avalanches, tsunamis, subsidence and liquefaction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: River floods, flash floods, urban floods and dam-break floods are classified as:

options.A: Geological hazards
options.B: Hydrological hazards
options.C: Climatological hazards

questions.explanation: Hydrological hazards include river floods, flash floods, urban and coastal floods, dam-break floods and water-related scarcity.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Cyclones, severe storms, tornadoes, thunderstorms, lightning and hailstorms are examples of:

options.A: Geological hazards
options.B: Hydrological hazards
options.C: Meteorological hazards

questions.explanation: Meteorological hazards include cyclones, severe storms, tornadoes, thunderstorms, lightning, hailstorms and extreme rainfall.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Drought, heatwaves, cold waves and prolonged wildfire conditions are classified as:

options.A: Meteorological hazards
options.B: Climatological hazards
options.C: Biological hazards

questions.explanation: Climatological hazards include drought, heatwaves, cold waves, prolonged wildfire conditions and desertification.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Epidemics, pandemics, vector-borne disease outbreaks and pest attacks are classified as:

options.A: Biological hazards
options.B: Climatological hazards
options.C: Technological hazards

questions.explanation: Biological hazards include epidemics, pandemics, vector-borne disease outbreaks, animal and crop disease and pest attacks.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Industrial accidents, chemical leaks, transport accidents, oil spills and nuclear incidents are examples of:

options.A: Natural hazards
options.B: Human-induced or technological hazards
options.C: Biological hazards

questions.explanation: Human-induced or technological hazards include industrial and chemical accidents, fires, transport accidents, structural failures, oil spills, nuclear/radiological incidents and conflict-related emergencies.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What are natural disasters?

options.A: Disasters caused only by human activity
options.B: Disasters triggered by natural processes such as earthquakes, cyclones, floods, droughts, landslides, epidemics and wildfires
options.C: Disasters that occur only in coastal areas
options.D: Disasters that never involve human factors

questions.explanation: Natural disasters are triggered by natural processes. However, human actions can increase their probability or impacts, such as deforestation intensifying landslide risk and unplanned urbanisation worsening flooding.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What are human-induced disasters?

options.A: Disasters caused by natural processes only
options.B: Disasters caused or substantially triggered by human activity such as industrial accidents, chemical leaks, dam failures, transport accidents and oil spills
options.C: Disasters that occur only in rural areas
options.D: Disasters that cannot combine with natural factors

questions.explanation: Human-induced disasters are caused or substantially triggered by human activity. Natural and human factors can combine, as in a flood worsened by blocked drains or a landslide triggered by slope cutting.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of human action amplifying a natural hazard?

options.A: Deforestation intensifying landslide risk
options.B: Earthquake generating seismic waves
options.C: Volcanic eruption releasing magma
options.D: Cyclone forming over warm ocean water

questions.explanation: Human actions can increase the probability or impacts of natural hazards; for example, deforestation can intensify landslide risk and unplanned urbanisation can worsen flooding.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Sudden-onset disasters are characterised by:

options.A: Gradual development over months or years
options.B: Rapid development, such as earthquakes, flash floods and explosions
options.C: Always providing long warning periods

questions.explanation: Sudden-onset events develop rapidly, such as earthquakes, flash floods and explosions.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a slow-onset hazard?

options.A: Earthquake
options.B: Flash flood
options.C: Drought

questions.explanation: Slow-onset hazards develop gradually, such as drought, desertification, sea-level rise and some epidemics.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about cyclones as hazards is correct?

options.A: They are slow-onset hazards with no warning
options.B: They provide warning but can still produce rapid impacts
options.C: They never cause rapid impacts
options.D: They are classified only as geological hazards

questions.explanation: Some hazards, such as cyclones, provide warning but can still produce rapid impacts.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a compound disaster?

options.A: A disaster caused by a single hazard only
options.B: A disaster involving multiple hazards or drivers occurring together or in sequence
options.C: A disaster that occurs only in urban areas
options.D: A disaster with no human impact

questions.explanation: A compound disaster involves multiple hazards or drivers occurring together or in sequence.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a cascading disaster?

options.A: A disaster that affects only one sector
options.B: A disaster that occurs when one event triggers secondary failures
options.C: A disaster that develops very slowly
options.D: A disaster caused only by climate change

questions.explanation: A cascading disaster occurs when one event triggers secondary failures, such as an earthquake causing landslides and dam damage.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a cascading disaster?

options.A: An earthquake causing landslides and dam damage
options.B: A single drought affecting one district
options.C: A heatwave lasting two days

questions.explanation: Examples of cascading disasters include an earthquake causing landslides and dam damage, or extreme rainfall causing floods, slope failures and power disruption.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) is best described as:

options.A: The provision of relief after a disaster
options.B: The systematic effort to prevent new risk, reduce existing risk and manage residual risk through policies, institutions, investment, preparedness and resilience-building
options.C: The construction of embankments only
options.D: The evacuation of people during a disaster

questions.explanation: DRR is the systematic effort to prevent new risk, reduce existing risk and manage residual risk through policies, institutions, investment, preparedness and resilience-building.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The primary aim of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) is to:

options.A: Increase exposure to hazards
options.B: Reduce disaster losses in lives, livelihoods, health, assets and ecosystems
options.C: Maximise disaster response time
options.D: Replace all structural measures with relief

questions.explanation: DRR aims to reduce disaster losses in lives, livelihoods, health, assets and ecosystems.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is an earthquake?

options.A: Ground shaking caused by the sudden release of energy within the Earth, commonly due to slip along a fault
options.B: A large ocean wave caused by wind
options.C: The downslope movement of rock and debris
options.D: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation

questions.explanation: An earthquake is ground shaking caused by the sudden release of energy within the Earth, commonly due to slip along a fault as tectonic stress accumulates.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Besides tectonic fault slip, which of the following can cause earthquakes?

options.A: Volcanic activity, collapse and some human activities such as mining or fluid injection
options.B: Only wind action
options.C: Only rainfall

questions.explanation: Other causes of earthquakes include volcanic activity, collapse and some human activities such as mining or fluid injection.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The focus or hypocentre of an earthquake is:

options.A: The point on the Earth's surface vertically above the epicentre
options.B: The point within the Earth where rupture begins
options.C: The point of maximum damage on the surface

questions.explanation: The focus or hypocentre is the point within the Earth where rupture begins.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The epicentre of an earthquake is:

options.A: The point within the Earth where rupture begins
options.B: The point on the Earth's surface vertically above the focus
options.C: The deepest point of the fault
options.D: The point where seismic waves are recorded

questions.explanation: The epicentre is the point on the Earth's surface vertically above the focus.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Shaking severity at a location during an earthquake depends on:

options.A: Depth, magnitude, distance, local ground conditions and building vulnerability
options.B: Only the magnitude of the earthquake
options.C: Only the distance from the epicentre

questions.explanation: Shaking severity at a location depends on depth, magnitude, distance, local ground conditions and building vulnerability.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which earthquake waves are compressional and travel through solids, liquids and gases?

options.A: S waves
options.B: P waves
options.C: Love waves

questions.explanation: P waves are compressional and travel through solids, liquids and gases.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which earthquake waves are shear waves that travel through solids but not liquids?

options.A: P waves
options.B: S waves
options.C: Surface waves

questions.explanation: S waves are shear waves and travel through solids but not liquids.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which earthquake waves travel along the surface and often cause severe structural damage?

options.A: P waves
options.B: S waves
options.C: Surface waves (Love and Rayleigh)

questions.explanation: Surface waves (Love and Rayleigh) travel along the surface and often cause severe structural damage.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Earthquake magnitude is:

options.A: A measure of observed shaking and damage at a particular place
options.B: An estimate of the size of the earthquake source, expressed using scales such as moment magnitude (Mw)
options.C: A measure of the depth of the focus only

questions.explanation: Magnitude estimates the size of the earthquake source and is expressed using scales such as moment magnitude (Mw).

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Earthquake intensity describes:

options.A: The size of the earthquake source
options.B: Observed shaking and damage at a particular place, commonly using the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale
options.C: The depth of the hypocentre

questions.explanation: Intensity describes observed shaking and damage at a particular place, commonly using the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale. One earthquake has one magnitude but varying local intensities.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates earthquake magnitude and intensity?

options.A: One earthquake has one magnitude but varying local intensities
options.B: One earthquake has one intensity but varying magnitudes
options.C: Magnitude and intensity are identical measures
options.D: Intensity measures the source size while magnitude measures damage

questions.explanation: Magnitude estimates the size of the earthquake source; intensity describes observed shaking and damage at a particular place. One earthquake has one magnitude but varying local intensities.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a volcanic eruption?

options.A: The release of magma, gases and volcanic material at the surface
options.B: The downslope movement of rock and debris
options.C: A series of long-wavelength sea waves
options.D: The sinking of the ground surface

questions.explanation: A volcanic eruption is the release of magma, gases and volcanic material at the surface.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a volcanic hazard?

options.A: Lava flows
options.B: Ash fall
options.C: Pyroclastic density currents

questions.explanation: Volcanic hazards include lava flows, ash fall, pyroclastic density currents, lahars, toxic gases and, in some settings, volcanic tsunamis. Soil liquefaction is associated with earthquake shaking.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The only confirmed historically active volcano in India is:

options.A: Narcondam Island
options.B: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea
options.C: Deccan Traps

questions.explanation: The only confirmed historically active volcano in India is Barren Island in the Andaman Sea.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a landslide?

options.A: The downslope movement of rock, debris or earth under gravity
options.B: The sudden release of energy within the Earth
options.C: A series of long-wavelength sea waves
options.D: The gradual sinking of the ground surface

questions.explanation: A landslide is the downslope movement of rock, debris or earth under gravity.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of landslide?

options.A: Falls
options.B: Topples
options.C: Spreads

questions.explanation: Landslide types include falls, topples, slides, spreads and flows. Liquefaction is a separate phenomenon associated with earthquake shaking in saturated loose granular soil.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a trigger for landslides?

options.A: Intense or prolonged rainfall
options.B: Earthquakes
options.C: Slope cutting and deforestation

questions.explanation: Triggers of landslides include intense or prolonged rainfall, earthquakes, slope cutting, deforestation, mining and poor drainage.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Why are landslides common in steep, wet mountain regions?

options.A: Steep slopes increase gravitational stress; weathered or fractured material can lose strength when saturated; intense rainfall raises pore-water pressure; and road cuts or construction can destabilise slopes
options.B: Because these regions have no vegetation at all
options.C: Because earthquakes never occur there
options.D: Because the rock is always dry and strong

questions.explanation: Steep slopes increase gravitational stress; weathered or fractured material can lose strength when saturated; intense rainfall raises pore-water pressure; and road cuts or construction can destabilise slopes. Geology, drainage, vegetation and land-use decisions all influence susceptibility.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which factors influence landslide susceptibility in mountain regions?

options.A: Geology, drainage, vegetation and land-use decisions
options.B: Only rainfall intensity
options.C: Only slope angle

questions.explanation: Geology, drainage, vegetation and land-use decisions all influence susceptibility to landslides.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is an avalanche?

options.A: A rapid downslope movement of snow, sometimes carrying ice, rock and debris
options.B: A series of long-wavelength sea waves
options.C: The sinking of the ground surface

questions.explanation: An avalanche is a rapid downslope movement of snow, sometimes carrying ice, rock and debris. It is associated mainly with steep snow-covered mountain slopes.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can trigger an avalanche?

options.A: Heavy snowfall and wind loading
options.B: Warming and rain-on-snow
options.C: Disturbance of the snowpack

questions.explanation: Heavy snowfall, wind loading, warming, rain-on-snow and disturbance can trigger avalanches.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a tsunami?

options.A: A series of long-wavelength sea waves generated by sudden displacement of a large water volume
options.B: A rotating low-pressure weather system over warm oceans
options.C: An abnormal rise of seawater above the predicted astronomical tide
options.D: A rapidly rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm to the ground

questions.explanation: A tsunami is a series of long-wavelength sea waves generated by sudden displacement of a large water volume, most often by undersea earthquakes, but also by submarine landslides or volcanic events.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is the most common cause of a tsunami?

options.A: Daily sea breeze
options.B: Sudden displacement of a large water volume, most often by undersea earthquakes
options.C: Ordinary wind waves

questions.explanation: Tsunamis are most often generated by undersea earthquakes, but also by submarine landslides or volcanic events.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: How does a tsunami behave as it travels from deep water to the shore?

options.A: It travels rapidly with small wave height in deep water and slows and can rise dramatically near shore
options.B: It travels slowly in deep water and speeds up near shore
options.C: It maintains the same wave height everywhere
options.D: It disappears completely in shallow water

questions.explanation: In deep water a tsunami may travel rapidly with small wave height; near shore it slows and can rise dramatically.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates a tsunami from ordinary wind waves?

options.A: Wind waves are generated mainly by wind acting on the sea surface and have relatively short wavelengths, while tsunamis involve movement of the water column over very long wavelengths
options.B: Tsunamis are generated by wind and have short wavelengths
options.C: Wind waves are generated by undersea earthquakes
options.D: Tsunamis and wind waves are identical in wavelength and generation

questions.explanation: Wind waves are generated mainly by wind acting on the sea surface and have relatively short wavelengths. Tsunamis involve the movement of the water column over very long wavelengths and are generated by sudden displacement of water.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is ground subsidence?

options.A: The gradual or sudden sinking of the ground surface due to underground material movement or loss of support
options.B: The downslope movement of rock and debris
options.C: The temporary overflow of water onto dry land
options.D: The loss of effective strength in saturated soil during shaking

questions.explanation: Ground subsidence is the gradual or sudden sinking of the ground surface due to underground material movement or loss of support.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a cause of ground subsidence?

options.A: Groundwater or hydrocarbon withdrawal
options.B: Mining and dissolution of soluble rocks
options.C: Natural compaction and underground construction

questions.explanation: Causes of ground subsidence include groundwater or hydrocarbon withdrawal, mining, dissolution of soluble rocks, natural compaction and underground construction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is soil liquefaction?

options.A: During strong shaking, saturated loose granular soil loses effective strength as pore-water pressure rises, causing it to behave temporarily like a liquid
options.B: The permanent freezing of soil in cold regions
options.C: The erosion of soil by flowing water
options.D: The compaction of dry sand under static load

questions.explanation: During strong shaking, saturated loose granular soil can lose effective strength as pore-water pressure rises, causing it to behave temporarily like a liquid.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Soil liquefaction is most likely in:

options.A: Dry solid granite
options.B: Saturated loose granular soil during strong shaking
options.C: Hard crystalline rock

questions.explanation: Rising pore-water pressure can reduce effective stress in saturated loose granular soil during strong shaking.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a consequence of soil liquefaction?

options.A: Building settlement and tilting
options.B: Lateral spreading
options.C: Damage to buried infrastructure

questions.explanation: Liquefaction may lead to building settlement, tilting, lateral spreading and damage to buried infrastructure.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following measures helps reduce geological disaster risk?

options.A: Use seismic and landslide hazard maps and enforce earthquake-resistant building codes
options.B: Avoid construction on unstable slopes and active fault zones
options.C: Maintain drainage and regulate slope cutting and mining

questions.explanation: Geological disaster risk can be reduced by using seismic and landslide hazard maps; enforcing earthquake-resistant building codes; avoiding construction on unstable slopes and active fault zones; maintaining drainage; regulating slope cutting and mining; monitoring volcanoes and snow conditions; providing public warning and evacuation plans; and protecting critical infrastructure.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a flood?

options.A: The temporary overflow of water onto land that is normally dry
options.B: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation
options.C: The downslope movement of rock and debris
options.D: An abnormal rise of seawater above the predicted tide

questions.explanation: A flood is the temporary overflow of water onto land that is normally dry. It may result from intense rainfall, river overflow, storm surge, rapid snowmelt, dam failure or drainage obstruction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can cause a flood?

options.A: Intense rainfall and river overflow
options.B: Storm surge and rapid snowmelt
options.C: Dam failure and drainage obstruction

questions.explanation: Floods may result from intense rainfall, river overflow, storm surge, rapid snowmelt, dam failure or drainage obstruction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a flash flood?

options.A: A rapid flood that develops within a short period after intense rainfall, dam or embankment failure, or sudden release of water
options.B: A flood that develops gradually over several weeks
options.C: A long-term climatic condition of low moisture
options.D: An abnormal rise of seawater associated with a cyclone

questions.explanation: A flash flood is a rapid flood that develops within a short period after intense rainfall, dam or embankment failure, or sudden release of water.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Why are flash floods particularly dangerous in steep catchments, narrow valleys and urban areas?

options.A: Because warning time may be very limited
options.B: Because they always occur at night
options.C: Because they never cause damage

questions.explanation: Flash floods are particularly dangerous in steep catchments, narrow valleys and urban areas because warning time may be very limited.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: A river flood occurs when:

options.A: River discharge exceeds channel capacity and water spills onto the floodplain
options.B: Rainfall is below normal for a long period
options.C: Seawater rises above the predicted tide

questions.explanation: A river flood occurs when river discharge exceeds channel capacity and water spills onto the floodplain.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can contribute to a river flood?

options.A: Prolonged rainfall and saturated soils
options.B: Snowmelt and upstream inflows
options.C: Reservoir operations

questions.explanation: Prolonged rainfall, saturated soils, snowmelt, upstream inflows and reservoir operations can contribute to river floods.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is urban flooding?

options.A: Flooding in built-up areas when rainfall runoff exceeds the capacity of drains, streams and storage systems
options.B: Flooding caused only by storm surge
options.C: Flooding caused only by dam failure
options.D: Flooding that occurs only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Urban flooding is flooding in built-up areas when rainfall runoff exceeds the capacity of drains, streams and storage systems.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following increases urban flood risk?

options.A: Impervious surfaces and encroached lakes and floodplains
options.B: Blocked drains and inadequate maintenance
options.C: Unplanned development

questions.explanation: Impervious surfaces, encroached lakes and floodplains, blocked drains, inadequate maintenance and unplanned development increase urban flood risk.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is coastal flooding?

options.A: Inundation of coastal land due to storm surge, high tides, waves, extreme rainfall, river discharge or sea-level rise
options.B: Flooding caused only by river overflow
options.C: Flooding caused only by dam failure
options.D: The temporary overflow of water onto land that is normally dry

questions.explanation: Coastal flooding is the inundation of coastal land due to storm surge, high tides, waves, extreme rainfall, river discharge or sea-level rise.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Cyclones can produce destructive storm surges especially along:

options.A: Low-lying coasts and estuaries
options.B: High mountain ridges
options.C: Dry desert interiors

questions.explanation: Cyclones can produce destructive storm surges, especially along low-lying coasts and estuaries.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a storm surge?

options.A: An abnormal rise of seawater above the predicted astronomical tide, driven mainly by strong winds and low atmospheric pressure associated with a storm
options.B: A series of long-wavelength sea waves generated by undersea earthquakes
options.C: An ordinary wind wave generated by sea breeze
options.D: A temporary overflow of river water onto the floodplain

questions.explanation: A storm surge is an abnormal rise of seawater above the predicted astronomical tide, driven mainly by strong winds and low atmospheric pressure associated with a storm.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: A storm surge coinciding with high tide can:

options.A: Worsen coastal inundation
options.B: Reduce coastal flooding
options.C: Have no effect on coastal flooding

questions.explanation: Surge coinciding with high tide can worsen coastal inundation.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a major impact of floods?

options.A: Deaths, injuries and displacement
options.B: Crop and livestock loss and damage to homes and infrastructure
options.C: Contamination of drinking water, disease risk, erosion and sediment deposition

questions.explanation: Flood impacts include deaths and injuries, displacement, crop and livestock loss, damage to homes and infrastructure, contamination of drinking water, disease risk, erosion, sediment deposition, disruption of transport and economic losses.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a positive effect of floods under natural conditions?

options.A: They can replenish floodplain soils and wetlands
options.B: They always destroy all infrastructure
options.C: They cause permanent drought

questions.explanation: Floods can also replenish floodplain soils and wetlands under natural conditions.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is drought?

options.A: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation relative to the local normal, leading to water shortage
options.B: A temporary overflow of water onto dry land
options.C: An abnormal rise of seawater above the predicted tide
options.D: The downslope movement of rock and debris

questions.explanation: Drought is a prolonged period of deficient precipitation relative to the local normal, leading to water shortage.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Drought is commonly classified as:

options.A: Meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and socio-economic
options.B: Geological, hydrological and biological
options.C: Sudden and slow-onset only

questions.explanation: Drought is commonly classified as meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and socio-economic.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Meteorological drought is indicated by:

options.A: Precipitation deficit relative to a defined climatological normal
options.B: Soil-moisture deficit affecting crops
options.C: Below-normal streamflow, reservoir storage, lake levels or groundwater
options.D: Water shortage affecting production and demand-supply systems

questions.explanation: Meteorological drought is a precipitation deficit relative to a defined climatological normal.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Agricultural drought is indicated by:

options.A: Precipitation deficit relative to a climatological normal
options.B: Soil-moisture deficit affecting crops, pasture and plant growth
options.C: Below-normal streamflow and reservoir storage

questions.explanation: Agricultural drought is a soil-moisture deficit affecting crops, pasture and plant growth.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Hydrological drought is indicated by:

options.A: Precipitation deficit relative to a climatological normal
options.B: Soil-moisture deficit affecting crops
options.C: Below-normal streamflow, reservoir storage, lake levels or groundwater
options.D: Water shortage affecting production and demand-supply systems

questions.explanation: Hydrological drought is indicated by below-normal streamflow, reservoir storage, lake levels or groundwater.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Socio-economic drought is indicated by:

options.A: Precipitation deficit relative to a climatological normal
options.B: Soil-moisture deficit affecting crops
options.C: Below-normal streamflow and reservoir storage
options.D: Water shortage affecting people, livelihoods, production and demand-supply systems

questions.explanation: Socio-economic drought occurs when water shortage affects people, livelihoods, production and demand-supply systems.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is the difference between drought and aridity?

options.A: Drought is a temporary or episodic precipitation and water-availability deficit; aridity is a long-term climatic condition of low moisture availability
options.B: Drought is a long-term climatic condition; aridity is temporary
options.C: Drought and aridity are identical terms
options.D: Aridity occurs only in humid regions

questions.explanation: Drought is a temporary or episodic precipitation and water-availability deficit relative to local climate. Aridity is a long-term climatic condition of low moisture availability. A naturally arid region can experience drought, but the terms are not interchangeable.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: A long-term climatic condition of low moisture availability is:

options.A: Drought
options.B: Aridity
options.C: Flood

questions.explanation: Aridity is a persistent climate characteristic; drought is episodic.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is water scarcity?

options.A: When available usable water is insufficient to meet demand or when poor quality, access, infrastructure or governance prevents people and ecosystems from obtaining adequate water
options.B: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation only
options.C: A temporary overflow of water onto dry land
options.D: The downslope movement of water-saturated soil

questions.explanation: Water scarcity occurs when available usable water is insufficient to meet demand or when poor quality, access, infrastructure or governance prevents people and ecosystems from obtaining adequate water. It can be physical or economic.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Water scarcity can be:

options.A: Physical or economic
options.B: Only physical
options.C: Only economic

questions.explanation: Water scarcity can be physical or economic.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can cause a dam failure?

options.A: Structural defects and poor design or construction
options.B: Inadequate maintenance and foundation problems
options.C: Overtopping, extreme floods, internal erosion or piping, landslides, earthquakes, gate malfunction and operational errors

questions.explanation: Dam failures can be caused by structural defects, poor design or construction, inadequate maintenance, foundation problems, overtopping, extreme floods, internal erosion or piping, landslides, earthquakes, gate malfunction and operational errors.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Dam-break floods are particularly dangerous because:

options.A: They can travel rapidly downstream
options.B: They always occur slowly
options.C: They affect only the dam site
options.D: They never cause loss of life

questions.explanation: Dam-break floods can travel rapidly downstream.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a measure for managing flood risk?

options.A: Floodplain zoning and restoring wetlands and natural drainage
options.B: Maintaining lakes, tanks and channels and improving stormwater systems
options.C: Catchment treatment, flood forecasting and evacuation plans

questions.explanation: Flood risk can be managed by floodplain zoning; restoring wetlands and natural drainage; maintaining lakes, tanks and channels; improving stormwater systems; catchment treatment; embankments and reservoirs where appropriate; flood forecasting; evacuation plans; resilient infrastructure; and community awareness.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a measure for managing drought risk?

options.A: Rainwater harvesting, watershed development, groundwater recharge and regulation
options.B: Efficient irrigation, drought-resilient crops, soil-moisture conservation and crop diversification
options.C: Drinking-water contingency plans, fodder banks and timely agricultural advisories

questions.explanation: Drought risk can be managed through rainwater harvesting, watershed development, groundwater recharge and regulation, efficient irrigation, drought-resilient crops, soil-moisture conservation, crop diversification, drinking-water contingency plans, fodder banks and timely agricultural advisories.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a tropical cyclone?

options.A: A rotating low-pressure weather system that develops over sufficiently warm tropical or subtropical oceans, with organised convection and a closed circulation
options.B: A violently rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm cloud to the ground
options.C: A period of unusually high temperature relative to local climatology
options.D: A rapid downslope movement of snow

questions.explanation: A tropical cyclone is a rotating low-pressure weather system that develops over sufficiently warm tropical or subtropical oceans, with organised convection and a closed circulation.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can a tropical cyclone cause?

options.A: Destructive winds
options.B: Torrential rain
options.C: Storm surge and coastal flooding

questions.explanation: A tropical cyclone can cause destructive winds, torrential rain, storm surge and coastal flooding.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Regional names for tropical cyclones include:

options.A: Hurricane, typhoon and cyclone
options.B: Tornado, twister and whirlwind
options.C: Tsunami, surge and swell

questions.explanation: Regional names for tropical cyclones include hurricane, typhoon and cyclone.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following conditions favours tropical cyclone formation?

options.A: Warm ocean water and abundant moisture
options.B: Atmospheric instability and low vertical wind shear
options.C: Sufficient Coriolis force away from the equator and a pre-existing low-level disturbance

questions.explanation: Conditions favouring tropical cyclone formation include warm ocean water, abundant moisture, atmospheric instability, sufficient Coriolis force away from the equator, low vertical wind shear and a pre-existing low-level disturbance. No single factor guarantees formation.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about tropical cyclone formation is correct?

options.A: No single factor guarantees formation
options.B: Warm ocean water alone guarantees formation
options.C: Cyclones form only near the equator where Coriolis force is zero
options.D: High vertical wind shear favours formation

questions.explanation: Several conditions favour tropical cyclone formation, but no single factor guarantees formation.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: In a mature tropical cyclone, the relatively calm central region is called the:

options.A: Eyewall
options.B: Eye
options.C: Spiral rainband

questions.explanation: The eye is the relatively calm central region of a mature tropical cyclone.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The eyewall of a tropical cyclone:

options.A: Surrounds the eye and contains intense winds and rainfall
options.B: Is the calm central region
options.C: Is the outermost region with no rainfall
options.D: Is the region of weakest winds

questions.explanation: The eyewall surrounds the eye and contains intense winds and rainfall.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: In a mature tropical cyclone, the strongest winds are generally found:

options.A: In the eye
options.B: Near the eyewall
options.C: In the outermost spiral rainbands
options.D: At the centre of the eye

questions.explanation: The strongest winds are generally near the eyewall, not the eye.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Spiral rainbands in a tropical cyclone:

options.A: Extend outward from the eyewall
options.B: Are located only inside the eye
options.C: Do not produce any rainfall
options.D: Are the calmest part of the storm

questions.explanation: Spiral rainbands extend outward from the eyewall.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a severe storm?

options.A: A storm with hazardous conditions such as damaging winds, intense rainfall, hail, lightning or coastal surge
options.B: A period of unusually high temperature
options.C: A series of long-wavelength sea waves
options.D: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation

questions.explanation: A severe storm has hazardous conditions such as damaging winds, intense rainfall, hail, lightning or coastal surge. Severe-storm definitions and warning thresholds differ among national meteorological agencies.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Severe-storm definitions and warning thresholds:

options.A: Are identical across all countries
options.B: Differ among national meteorological agencies
options.C: Are set only by the United Nations

questions.explanation: Severe-storm definitions and warning thresholds differ among national meteorological agencies.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a tornado?

options.A: A violently rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm cloud to the ground
options.B: A rotating low-pressure weather system over warm oceans
options.C: A series of long-wavelength sea waves
options.D: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation

questions.explanation: A tornado is a violently rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm cloud to the ground.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Compared with tropical cyclones, tornadoes are usually:

options.A: Much smaller in spatial extent and shorter-lived, but can produce extremely intense local winds
options.B: Much larger and longer-lived
options.C: Identical in size and duration

questions.explanation: Tornadoes are usually much smaller in spatial extent and shorter-lived than tropical cyclones, but can produce extremely intense local winds.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a thunderstorm?

options.A: A convective storm associated with cumulonimbus clouds, lightning and thunder, often with heavy rain, gusty winds and sometimes hail or tornadoes
options.B: A rotating low-pressure weather system over warm oceans
options.C: A period of unusually low minimum temperature

questions.explanation: A thunderstorm is a convective storm associated with cumulonimbus clouds, lightning and thunder, often with heavy rain, gusty winds and sometimes hail or tornadoes.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Strong updrafts and downdrafts in a thunderstorm develop due to:

options.A: Atmospheric instability
options.B: Low ocean salinity
options.C: High soil moisture

questions.explanation: Strong updrafts and downdrafts develop due to atmospheric instability.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What causes lightning?

options.A: An electrical discharge caused by charge separation within a thunderstorm cloud or between cloud and ground
options.B: The sudden release of energy within the Earth
options.C: The rapid downslope movement of snow
options.D: The overflow of water onto dry land

questions.explanation: Lightning is an electrical discharge caused by charge separation within a thunderstorm cloud or between cloud and ground.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can lightning cause?

options.A: Death and injuries
options.B: Fires and power-system damage
options.C: Injuries even outside the heaviest rainfall

questions.explanation: Lightning can cause death, fires, power-system damage and injuries even outside the heaviest rainfall.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a hailstorm?

options.A: A storm that produces balls or irregular lumps of ice formed when strong thunderstorm updrafts carry supercooled water droplets upward
options.B: A storm that produces only lightning
options.C: A storm that produces only strong winds
options.D: A storm that produces only heavy rainfall

questions.explanation: A hailstorm produces hailstones formed when strong thunderstorm updrafts carry supercooled water droplets upward, allowing layers of ice to accumulate.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Hail can damage:

options.A: Crops
options.B: Vehicles and roofs
options.C: People

questions.explanation: Hail can damage crops, vehicles, roofs and people.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a heatwave?

options.A: A period of unusually high temperature relative to local climatology, often lasting several days and posing health and livelihood risks
options.B: A period of unusually low minimum temperature
options.C: A very intense rainfall event over a small area

questions.explanation: A heatwave is a period of unusually high temperature relative to local climatology, often lasting several days and posing health and livelihood risks.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: In India, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) uses heatwave criteria based on:

options.A: Region-specific maximum temperature and departure from normal
options.B: Only minimum night temperature
options.C: Only rainfall deficit

questions.explanation: In India, IMD uses region-specific criteria based on maximum temperature and departure from normal; exact operational thresholds should be checked in current IMD guidance.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a cold wave?

options.A: A period of unusually low minimum temperature or a substantial fall below normal, defined using region-specific meteorological criteria
options.B: A period of unusually high temperature
options.C: A very intense rainfall event over a small area

questions.explanation: A cold wave is a period of unusually low minimum temperature or a substantial fall below normal, defined using region-specific meteorological criteria.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following can a cold wave cause?

options.A: Hypothermia and respiratory stress
options.B: Crop damage
options.C: Livestock losses

questions.explanation: A cold wave can cause hypothermia, respiratory stress, crop damage and livestock losses.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a cloudburst?

options.A: A very intense rainfall event over a small area in a short time
options.B: A period of unusually low temperature
options.C: A violently rotating column of air

questions.explanation: A cloudburst is a very intense rainfall event over a small area in a short time. The term is commonly used in India for extremely heavy localised rainfall, especially in hilly terrain.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: A cloudburst can trigger:

options.A: Flash floods
options.B: Debris flows
options.C: Landslides

questions.explanation: A cloudburst can trigger flash floods, debris flows and landslides; exact operational definitions vary.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following are dangers of heavy rainfall?

options.A: Riverine and flash flooding and urban inundation
options.B: Landslides and soil erosion
options.C: Crop damage, water contamination, transport disruption and reservoir inflow surges

questions.explanation: Dangers of heavy rainfall include riverine and flash flooding, urban inundation, landslides, soil erosion, crop damage, water contamination, transport disruption and reservoir inflow surges.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Impacts of heavy rainfall are determined by:

options.A: Rainfall intensity, duration, antecedent soil moisture and catchment characteristics
options.B: Only rainfall intensity
options.C: Only wind speed

questions.explanation: Rainfall intensity, duration, antecedent soil moisture and catchment characteristics determine impacts of heavy rainfall.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a forest fire or wildfire?

options.A: An uncontrolled fire in vegetation
options.B: A period of unusually high temperature
options.C: A very intense rainfall event

questions.explanation: A forest fire or wildfire is an uncontrolled fire in vegetation. It may be surface, ground or crown fire.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Forest fire behaviour is determined by:

options.A: Weather, fuel load, terrain, ignition sources and vegetation type
options.B: Only wind speed
options.C: Only rainfall

questions.explanation: Weather, fuel load, terrain, ignition sources and vegetation type determine forest fire behaviour.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about forest fires is correct?

options.A: Some ecosystems are fire-adapted, but frequent or intense fires can cause severe degradation
options.B: All forest fires are always harmful to every ecosystem
options.C: Forest fires never occur in fire-adapted ecosystems
options.D: Forest fires are always caused by lightning only

questions.explanation: Some ecosystems are fire-adapted, but frequent or intense fires can cause severe degradation.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Forest fire prevention is best described as:

options.A: Reducing ignition and fuel-related risk through awareness, regulation, landscape management and early detection
options.B: The operational action to contain and extinguish a fire once it occurs
options.C: The restoration of burnt forests only
options.D: The evacuation of people during a fire

questions.explanation: Prevention reduces ignition and fuel-related risk through awareness, regulation, landscape management and early detection.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Forest fire suppression is best described as:

options.A: The operational action to contain and extinguish a fire once it occurs, prioritising life safety and safe tactics
options.B: Reducing ignition and fuel-related risk through awareness and regulation
options.C: The restoration of burnt forests only

questions.explanation: Suppression is the operational action to contain and extinguish a fire once it occurs, prioritising life safety and safe tactics.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is desertification?

options.A: Land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas caused by climatic variations and human activities
options.B: The natural expansion of deserts only
options.C: A prolonged period of deficient precipitation
options.D: The temporary overflow of water onto dry land

questions.explanation: Desertification is land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas caused by climatic variations and human activities. It involves loss of biological or economic productivity and is not simply the natural expansion of deserts.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about desertification is correct?

options.A: It is simply the natural expansion of deserts
options.B: It involves loss of biological or economic productivity in dry areas and is not simply the natural expansion of deserts
options.C: It occurs only in humid tropical regions

questions.explanation: Desertification involves loss of biological or economic productivity and is not simply the natural expansion of deserts.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: How can heatwave impacts be reduced?

options.A: Use early warnings, public advisories, work-rest schedules, hydration and cooling shelters
options.B: Ignore temperature forecasts
options.C: Increase strenuous outdoor activity during the hottest hours
options.D: Avoid drinking water during the day

questions.explanation: Heatwave impacts can be reduced by using early warnings, public advisories, work-rest schedules, hydration and cooling shelters for heat.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: How can cold-wave impacts be reduced?

options.A: Provide warm shelters, appropriate clothing, health outreach and protection of vulnerable people and livestock
options.B: Ignore minimum temperature forecasts
options.C: Encourage outdoor exposure during the coldest hours

questions.explanation: Cold-wave impacts can be reduced through warm shelters, appropriate clothing, health outreach and protection of vulnerable people and livestock.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is an epidemic?

options.A: An occurrence of disease cases in a community or region clearly in excess of normal expectancy during a given period
options.B: A disease consistently present at an expected baseline
options.C: An epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or continents
options.D: A disease transmitted only by mosquitoes

questions.explanation: An epidemic is an occurrence of disease cases in a community or region clearly in excess of normal expectancy during a given period. The definition depends on disease, population and baseline.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is a pandemic?

options.A: An epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or continents and affects a large number of people
options.B: A disease consistently present at an expected baseline in a population
options.C: An occurrence of disease above normal expectancy in one district
options.D: A disease transmitted only by ticks

questions.explanation: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or continents and affects a large number of people. Pandemic status describes geographic spread, not necessarily disease severity.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Endemic disease is best defined as:

options.A: A disease consistently present at an expected baseline in a population or area
options.B: A disease occurrence above expected levels
options.C: An epidemic with extensive international or intercontinental spread
options.D: A disease that has been completely eradicated

questions.explanation: Endemic disease is consistently present at an expected baseline in a population or area.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates endemic, epidemic and pandemic?

options.A: Endemic is consistently present at an expected baseline; epidemic is occurrence above expected levels; pandemic is an epidemic with extensive international or intercontinental spread
options.B: Endemic is above expected levels; epidemic is consistently present; pandemic is a local outbreak
options.C: Endemic, epidemic and pandemic are identical terms
options.D: Pandemic describes severity only, not geographic spread

questions.explanation: Endemic disease is consistently present at an expected baseline in a population or area; epidemic is occurrence above expected levels; pandemic is an epidemic with extensive international or intercontinental spread.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Pandemic status describes:

options.A: Geographic spread, not necessarily disease severity
options.B: Disease severity only
options.C: The mortality rate only

questions.explanation: Pandemic status describes geographic spread, not necessarily disease severity.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What are vector-borne diseases?

options.A: Diseases transmitted by living vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, sandflies or fleas
options.B: Diseases caused by nutritional deficiency
options.C: Diseases transmitted only through contaminated water
options.D: Diseases caused by genetic mutation only

questions.explanation: Vector-borne diseases are transmitted by living vectors such as mosquitoes, ticks, sandflies or fleas.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a mosquito-borne disease?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Dengue
options.C: Chikungunya

questions.explanation: Malaria, dengue and chikungunya are mosquito-borne diseases. Japanese encephalitis is also mosquito-borne, and kala-azar is sandfly-borne.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Kala-azar is transmitted by:

options.A: Mosquitoes
options.B: Sandflies
options.C: Ticks

questions.explanation: Kala-azar is sandfly-borne. Malaria, dengue, chikungunya and Japanese encephalitis are mosquito-borne.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Control of vector-borne diseases requires:

options.A: Vector surveillance and habitat management
options.B: Personal protection
options.C: Health services

questions.explanation: Control of vector-borne diseases requires vector surveillance, habitat management, personal protection and health services.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Why can animal diseases become disasters?

options.A: They can cause mass livestock mortality, threaten food security and livelihoods, disrupt trade and sometimes infect humans
options.B: They affect only wild animals
options.C: They never affect food security
options.D: They are always harmless to humans

questions.explanation: Animal diseases can cause mass livestock mortality, threaten food security and livelihoods, disrupt trade and sometimes infect humans.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What are zoonoses?

options.A: Diseases transmissible between animals and humans
options.B: Diseases that affect only plants
options.C: Diseases caused only by malnutrition

questions.explanation: Zoonoses are diseases transmissible between animals and humans; examples include rabies and certain influenza infections.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a zoonotic disease?

options.A: Rabies
options.B: Certain influenza infections
options.C: Both A and B

questions.explanation: Zoonoses are diseases transmissible between animals and humans; examples include rabies and certain influenza infections.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What are crop diseases?

options.A: Diseases caused by pathogens such as fungi, bacteria, viruses and nematodes
options.B: Damage caused only by insects
options.C: Diseases transmitted only by mosquitoes

questions.explanation: Crop diseases are caused by pathogens such as fungi, bacteria, viruses and nematodes.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Pest attacks involve:

options.A: Insects, mites, rodents or other organisms damaging crops
options.B: Only fungal pathogens
options.C: Only viral pathogens

questions.explanation: Pest attacks involve insects, mites, rodents or other organisms damaging crops.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Crop diseases and pest attacks can cause:

options.A: Yield loss
options.B: Food-price instability
options.C: Livelihood stress

questions.explanation: Crop diseases and pest attacks can cause yield loss, food-price instability and livelihood stress.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is an invasive species in disaster and biosecurity management?

options.A: A non-native organism that establishes and spreads, causing or likely to cause ecological, economic or health harm
options.B: A native species that is economically important
options.C: A species that is endangered
options.D: A species that occurs only in zoos

questions.explanation: An invasive species is a non-native organism that establishes and spreads, causing or likely to cause ecological, economic or health harm.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Invasive species can:

options.A: Alter habitats and reduce native biodiversity
options.B: Damage crops
options.C: Increase management costs

questions.explanation: Invasive species can alter habitats, reduce native biodiversity, damage crops and increase management costs.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: How are biological disasters managed?

options.A: Disease surveillance, early detection, laboratory confirmation and reporting
options.B: Vaccination where available, infection prevention and vector control
options.C: Quarantine or movement controls when justified, risk communication, One Health coordination and continuity of essential services

questions.explanation: Biological disasters are managed through disease surveillance, early detection, laboratory confirmation, reporting, vaccination where available, infection prevention, vector control, quarantine or movement controls when justified, risk communication, One Health coordination and continuity of essential services.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is the One Health approach?

options.A: An integrated approach recognising that human, animal, plant and ecosystem health are interconnected
options.B: An approach that focuses only on human health
options.C: An approach that focuses only on animal health
options.D: An approach that ignores environmental health

questions.explanation: The One Health approach recognises that human, animal, plant and ecosystem health are interconnected.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The One Health approach encourages coordination across:

options.A: Public health, veterinary, agriculture, wildlife and environmental sectors
options.B: Only public health and veterinary sectors
options.C: Only agriculture and wildlife sectors

questions.explanation: One Health encourages coordination across public health, veterinary, agriculture, wildlife and environmental sectors to prevent and respond to health threats.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is disaster management?

options.A: A continuous and integrated process of planning, organising, coordinating and implementing measures for prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction
options.B: The provision of relief after a disaster only
options.C: The construction of embankments only
options.D: The evacuation of people during a disaster only

questions.explanation: Disaster management is a continuous and integrated process of planning, organising, coordinating and implementing measures for prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: The disaster management cycle is commonly shown as:

options.A: Mitigation/prevention → preparedness → response → recovery
options.B: Response → mitigation → preparedness → recovery
options.C: Recovery → response → preparedness → mitigation

questions.explanation: The cycle is commonly shown as mitigation/prevention → preparedness → response → recovery (rehabilitation and reconstruction), with lessons from recovery feeding back into risk reduction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about the disaster management cycle is correct?

options.A: In practice the phases overlap and are not strictly linear
options.B: The phases are strictly linear and never overlap
options.C: Response comes before preparedness

questions.explanation: In practice the phases overlap and are not strictly linear.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of prevention/mitigation measures?

options.A: Land-use zoning and building codes
options.B: Slope stabilization and floodplain protection
options.C: Both A and B

questions.explanation: Prevention/mitigation measures include land-use zoning, building codes, slope stabilization and floodplain protection.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of preparedness measures?

options.A: Plans, drills, stockpiles, training, warning protocols and evacuation routes
options.B: Search and rescue
options.C: Debris clearance and infrastructure repair

questions.explanation: Preparedness measures include plans, drills, stockpiles, training, warning protocols and evacuation routes.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of response measures?

options.A: Search and rescue, evacuation, first aid, shelters, food, water and emergency communication
options.B: Land-use zoning
options.C: Building codes

questions.explanation: Response measures include search and rescue, evacuation, first aid, shelters, food, water and emergency communication.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of recovery measures?

options.A: Debris clearance, livelihood restoration, infrastructure repair, psychosocial support and resilient reconstruction
options.B: Search and rescue
options.C: Evacuation

questions.explanation: Recovery measures include debris clearance, livelihood restoration, infrastructure repair, psychosocial support and resilient reconstruction.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Prevention in disaster management aims to:

options.A: Avoid creating disaster risk or prevent a hazard from causing impacts where possible
options.B: Reduce the severity or consequences of hazards that cannot be fully prevented
options.C: Provide relief after a disaster

questions.explanation: Prevention aims to avoid creating disaster risk or prevent a hazard from causing impacts where possible. Mitigation reduces the severity or consequences of hazards that cannot be fully prevented.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Mitigation in disaster management aims to:

options.A: Avoid creating disaster risk entirely
options.B: Reduce the severity or consequences of hazards that cannot be fully prevented
options.C: Provide immediate relief after a disaster

questions.explanation: Mitigation reduces the severity or consequences of hazards that cannot be fully prevented. Some frameworks use prevention and mitigation with overlapping meanings.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is disaster preparedness?

options.A: Measures taken before a disaster to ensure effective response, including hazard and vulnerability mapping, contingency plans, drills, trained teams, emergency supplies, communication systems, evacuation routes and public awareness
options.B: Actions during and immediately after an event to save lives
options.C: The process of restoring livelihoods after a disaster
options.D: Immediate assistance to meet urgent needs

questions.explanation: Disaster preparedness refers to measures taken before a disaster to ensure effective response.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is disaster response?

options.A: Actions during and immediately after an event to save lives, reduce health impacts, ensure public safety and meet basic needs
options.B: Measures taken before a disaster to ensure effective response
options.C: The process of restoring livelihoods after a disaster
options.D: Medium- to long-term restoration of essential services

questions.explanation: Disaster response includes actions during and immediately after an event to save lives, reduce health impacts, ensure public safety and meet basic needs.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Disaster response includes:

options.A: Warning dissemination and evacuation
options.B: Search and rescue and emergency medical care
options.C: Shelter, food, water and restoration of critical services

questions.explanation: Response includes warning dissemination, evacuation, search and rescue, emergency medical care, shelter, food, water and restoration of critical services.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is disaster recovery?

options.A: The process of restoring or improving livelihoods, health, economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets and systems after a disaster
options.B: Actions during an event to save lives
options.C: Measures taken before a disaster
options.D: Immediate assistance to meet urgent needs

questions.explanation: Disaster recovery is the process of restoring or improving livelihoods, health, economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets and systems after a disaster.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Build Back Better in disaster recovery seeks to:

options.A: Reproduce pre-disaster vulnerabilities exactly
options.B: Achieve safer and more resilient recovery rather than simply reproducing pre-disaster vulnerabilities
options.C: Delay all reconstruction indefinitely

questions.explanation: Build Back Better seeks safer and more resilient recovery rather than simply reproducing pre-disaster vulnerabilities.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is disaster relief?

options.A: Immediate assistance to meet urgent needs such as food, safe water, shelter, clothing, medical care, sanitation and protection
options.B: Long-term reconstruction of infrastructure
options.C: Measures taken before a disaster
options.D: The process of restoring livelihoods after a disaster

questions.explanation: Disaster relief is immediate assistance to meet urgent needs. Relief is one part of response and does not replace long-term recovery.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about disaster relief is correct?

options.A: Relief is one part of response and does not replace long-term recovery
options.B: Relief is the same as recovery
options.C: Relief is a preparedness measure
options.D: Relief replaces all other phases of disaster management

questions.explanation: Relief is one part of response and does not replace long-term recovery.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is rehabilitation in disaster management?

options.A: Medium- to long-term restoration of essential services, livelihoods, housing, social support and community functioning after the emergency phase
options.B: Immediate assistance to meet urgent needs
options.C: Actions during an event to save lives

questions.explanation: Rehabilitation is medium- to long-term restoration of essential services, livelihoods, housing, social support and community functioning after the emergency phase.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What are early warning systems?

options.A: Integrated systems that detect, forecast and communicate hazards and enable people and institutions to act in time
options.B: Systems that provide relief after a disaster
options.C: Systems that reconstruct infrastructure after a disaster
options.D: Systems that provide insurance payments after a disaster

questions.explanation: Early warning systems are integrated systems that detect, forecast and communicate hazards and enable people and institutions to act in time.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Effective early warning systems include:

options.A: Risk knowledge, monitoring and forecasting, warning dissemination, and preparedness to respond
options.B: Only monitoring and forecasting
options.C: Only warning dissemination

questions.explanation: Effective early warning systems include risk knowledge, monitoring and forecasting, warning dissemination, and preparedness to respond. A forecast alone is not a complete early warning system.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which statement about early warning systems is correct?

options.A: A forecast alone is not a complete early warning system
options.B: A forecast alone is a complete early warning system
options.C: Early warning systems do not require communication
options.D: Early warning systems do not require preparedness to respond

questions.explanation: Effective early warning systems require risk knowledge, monitoring and forecasting, warning dissemination, and preparedness to respond. A forecast alone is not a complete early warning system.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is risk assessment?

options.A: A systematic process of identifying hazards, analysing exposure and vulnerability, estimating likelihood and consequences, and evaluating risk to guide decisions
options.B: The provision of relief after a disaster
options.C: The reconstruction of infrastructure after a disaster
options.D: The evacuation of people during a disaster

questions.explanation: Risk assessment is a systematic process of identifying hazards, analysing exposure and vulnerability, estimating likelihood and consequences, and evaluating risk to guide decisions.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Risk assessment may use:

options.A: Historical data, hazard models and GIS
options.B: Field surveys and scenario analysis
options.C: Both A and B

questions.explanation: Risk assessment may use historical data, hazard models, GIS, field surveys and scenario analysis.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is vulnerability assessment?

options.A: Assessment of factors that make people or assets susceptible to harm, including building quality, poverty, age, disability, health, livelihood dependence, social exclusion, ecosystem degradation and limited access to information or services
options.B: Assessment of the size of an earthquake source
options.C: Assessment of rainfall intensity only
options.D: Assessment of relief requirements after a disaster

questions.explanation: Vulnerability assessment is the assessment of factors that make people or assets susceptible to harm.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Which of the following is a factor considered in vulnerability assessment?

options.A: Building quality and poverty
options.B: Age, disability and health
options.C: Livelihood dependence, social exclusion, ecosystem degradation and limited access to information or services

questions.explanation: Vulnerability assessment considers building quality, poverty, age, disability, health, livelihood dependence, social exclusion, ecosystem degradation and limited access to information or services.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: What is community participation in disaster management?

options.A: Involving local residents, panchayats, urban local bodies, volunteers, civil-society groups and local institutions in risk mapping, planning, warning dissemination, drills, response and recovery
options.B: Excluding local residents from disaster planning
options.C: Relying only on national agencies for all disaster management
options.D: Providing relief only after a disaster

questions.explanation: Community participation involves local residents, panchayats, urban local bodies, volunteers, civil-society groups and local institutions in risk mapping, planning, warning dissemination, drills, response and recovery. Local knowledge improves relevance and trust.

questions.subject: Disaster Management
questions.question: Community participation in disaster management improves:

options.A: Relevance and trust
options.B: Only the speed of relief distribution
options.C: Only the construction of embankments
